subject: DR controls & temporary carveout: BrightRoad multi-region failover (RTO/RPO specifics)
messages:
From: Andrea Chu <andrea@brightrd.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Vela <m.vela@brightrd.com>, BrightRoad Security <security@brightrd.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Request: DR carveout and controls for multi-region failover (RTO/RPO detail)

Priyom —

Thanks for the earlier demo. Our compliance and engineering teams need a concrete set of controls and an exception request for the multi-region failover behavior you outlined. Specifically we need:

- RTO and RPO commitments for the warm-standby path (core payment flows + non-PII services).
- Clear activation lead time / expected cold-start latency if warm standby cannot take traffic.
- Evidence of encryption-in-transit / at-rest during cross-region replication and any key custody notes.
- A short mitigation plan for the 72-hour window we expect to operate under the carveout (if granted).

Can you provide these as a document we can attach to our SOC / procurement review? I attached our current infra diagram (BR_prod_arch_v2.pdf) to show constraints (PCI segmentation limits cross-region replication for some data).

Prefer a short call this week if it helps — Marco and I are available Wed morning PT.

—Andrea
Andrea Chu
Head of Platform Security, BrightRoad Payments
andrea@brightrd.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Andrea Chu <andrea@brightrd.com>
Cc: Marco Vela <m.vela@brightrd.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: DR carveout and controls for multi-region failover (RTO/RPO detail)

Andrea — thanks for the diagram and clear list.

We can produce a scoped mitigation + exception package. Quick answers up front:
- Proposed temporary RTO (core payment path): 15 minutes from failover trigger to full throughput for auth/settlement (with degraded latency in minute 0-5 while caches warm).
- Proposed RPO: 5 minutes for non-PII operational state, and a policy of no cross-region replication of full cardholder data (we use tokenization & customer-side PII controls).
- Activation lead time: our warm-standby approach supports near-immediate routing (<1min) when KV cache is warm; for cold fallback the additional model/container init time is 8–12 minutes depending on peak batch size.

I started a shared doc and will attach our mitigation PDF. Can we take Wed 14 Apr 09:30 PT for a 30-min sync? I’ll bring the runbook extract and a short list of telemetry checks that validate readiness.

On Wed’s call I’d like to confirm which Buckets in BR_prod_arch_v2 must have zero cross-region replication (so we can carve them out explicitly).

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

From: Marco Vela <m.vela@brightrd.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: DR carveout and controls for multi-region failover (RTO/RPO detail)

On Tue, Apr 13, 2027 at 10:07 AM Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com> wrote:
> Andrea — thanks for the diagram and clear list.
>
> We can produce a scoped mitigation + exception package. Quick answers up front: ...

Thanks — Wed 09:30 PT works for us. A couple items from engineering side before the call:

- We cannot accept replication of full cardholder data outside our primary PCI zone. Any RPO that implies cross-region replication of that dataset is a show-stopper.
- For non-PII operational state we can tolerate up to 10 minutes RPO, but prefer 2–5 minutes.
- We need to understand the expected latency degradation during the 0–15 minute failover window for our payment-gateway (SLA for 95th percentile). If Redwood expects a 2x latency increase for the first 10 minutes, we need that documented to accept user-impact risk.

Also, procurement will want the exact window where BrightRoad is responsible for traffic diversion versus Redwood (operational ownership during failover). Please add an explicit responsibilities matrix.

—Marco
Marco Vela
Sr. Engineering Manager, BrightRoad Payments

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Andrea Chu <andrea@brightrd.com>, Marco Vela <m.vela@brightrd.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed mitigation & temporary carveout package (doc + runbook extract)

Andrea / Marco —

Attached: redwood-mitigation-plan-20270420.pdf (summary) and runbook-extract.txt (excerpts of activation steps). Highlights below — this is intentionally prescriptive so your procurement/compliance team can attach it to the exception request.

1) Scope of carveout (explicit):
- Carveout applies only to cross-region replication of BrightRoad raw cardholder data buckets (PCI-scoped). Tokenized payloads and non-PII operational state continue to replicate.

2) RTO / RPO commitments (temporary, 90-day trial window):
- Core payment path RTO: 15 minutes to restore end-to-end throughput with degraded latency expectations during minutes 0–5. We commit to 95th percentile latency not exceeding 2x normal baseline during minutes 0–10, and return to baseline by minute 15 under normal load.
- RPO for non-PII operational state: 5 minutes. For tokenized or pseudonymized data: 1–2 minutes.

3) Activation lead time & behavioral modes:
- Warm standby: <1 minute routing cutover when KV caches are warm.
- Cold fallback: additional initialization 8–12 minutes (model/container start + cache warm).

4) Controls & evidence we will provide:
- End-to-end test runbook (attached excerpts) with automated health-check endpoints and signed monotonic timestamps for replication offsets.
- Audit log extracts showing failover triggers and time-to-detect metrics.
- KMS usage notes: customer keys are supported via CMEK; cross-region replication uses ephemeral session keys with strict bucket-level encryption policies (details in PDF).

5) Operational responsibilities matrix:
- BrightRoad: trigger authorization to route traffic to standby, validate PCI carveouts, coordinate cutover windows for high-value batches.
- Redwood: execute routing, run mitigation runbook, provide 24/7 on-call contact and telemetry dashboard links, provide post-incident RCA within 72 hours.

6) Acceptance criteria for the 72-hour mitigation window (if invoked):
- Auto-escalation to on-call after 90 seconds of degraded health; initial mitigation steps executed within 5 minutes; telemetry indicating throughput restored to >=90% of baseline within 15 minutes.

Attachments include a short test matrix and sample log extracts. Two small callouts: we cannot replicate raw PCI outside your zone and we will add a hard constraint in the runbook to prevent accidental replication.

Please review and flag any items for redline. If this is acceptable in principle we can produce a one-page exception addendum for legal + procurement and push for DocuSign.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: redwood-mitigation-plan-20270420.pdf (PDF, 6 pages), runbook-extract.txt (text, 2 pages)

Priyom —

This reads well and addresses most of our asks. A few quick redlines from security/procurement: please explicitly call out the telemetry endpoints we will receive access to (HTTP health, replication-offset, and KMS event audit). Also expand the responsibilities matrix to include a single phone contact for Redwood on-call during the 72-hour window.

If you can add those two items we can route the one-page exception addendum through legal. Please also raise the DocuSign link when ready — I will need Marco to sign for engineering acceptance and our procurement lead to countersign.

Thanks — we’re comfortable moving to a trial carveout once those two items are added.

—Andrea
